newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Maize Board funds report due this week.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Maize Board funds report due this week.

text.p: The report on the future of funds amassed by the now-disbanded South African Maize Board is expected by the end of the week, Agriculture Department director-general Bongiwe Njobe-Mbuli said on Wednesday.

She told the parliamentary public accounts committee that the department wanted the funds to be used to pay off loans from the Land and Agriculture Bank. But the board wanted to place the monies in a trust, she said.
"We are awaiting the outcome of the Kassier Commission, which is due to report at the end of this week on what to do with that," she said.
The Maize Board owes the agriculture bank about 411 million rand in terms of overdraft facilities guaranteed by the department.
Njobe-Mbuli said guarantees by the department on loans to co-operatives for grain silos now totalled 110.5 million rand and were due to expire in 2016.
Asked how certain the government was that these loans would be repaid, she said that this depended on the future of agriculture and whether co-operatives converted into companies.

"We believe that if any of the co-operatives do go in for liquidation (to convert into companies), as a matter of good business practice, the first principle will be to pay off what is due to the state," she said.

The last loans for building silos were granted in 1987 and were part of the then government's policy of providing heavy financial support to co-operatives, usually involving only white farmers, to strengthen them.
